page: Amazon Web Services gr6f.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. The instance provisions 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It features a memory-dense footprint of 128.0 GB of DDR4 system RAM operating at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Acceleration is supplied by a partitioned NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU delivering 11 GB of VRAM. Ephemeral high-speed storage is integrated directly via a dedicated 450 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark measurements indicate specialized strengths alongside specific architectural bottlenecks. The instance achieves top-tier results in small and medium large language model prompt processing, recording 4224.69 tokens per second on a 135M model and 1052.79 tokens per second on a 7B model. Single-core compute capability is strong, evidenced by a stress-ng score of 2988.59. Conversely, multi-core computational throughput and general compute benchmarks, including Geekbench and PassMark, fall into the middle 50% tier. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths register in the bottom quartile, reflecting DDR4 architectural limits during sustained non-cached memory access cycles.

The qualitative cost-efficiency model favors scenarios requiring high system memory density coupled with entry-level GPU offloading, avoiding the overhead of full enterprise GPU configurations. However, workloads dependent on massive uncached memory bandwidth or full GPU resource isolation face measurable tradeoffs due to fractional GPU slicing and DDR4 throughput. Amazon Web Services gr6f.4xlarge is best suited for visual computing, graphics-intensive workloads, moderate-scale machine learning inference, real-time audio or video streaming pipelines, and memory-heavy database environments requiring local NVMe scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services gr6f.4xlarge is a memory-dense accelerated computing server configured with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) on an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. It pairs 128.0 GB of DDR4 system memory with a fractional NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU providing 11 GB of VRAM, a 450 GB local NVMe SSD, and 10 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing shows exceptional prompt processing rates for small and medium language models alongside strong single-core CPU execution. Multi-threaded processing and cached application benchmarks demonstrate consistent mid-tier behavior, though uncached large-block memory throughput remains constrained. The instance provides a cost-effective alternative to full GPU deployments by combining high RAM capacity with fractional accelerator hardware, making it well suited for graphics streaming, AI inference, and memory-intensive analytical workloads.
